Episode 148. Sword Emperor (1)
The Black Sea, the land of the five kings.
Sirone's expedition and Kiarl had been fighting for over twelve hours already.
Ozodok was completely unconscious and had been pushed far away by the aftermath of the battle, and Kiarl was constantly screaming, spreading the energy of chaos.
The chaos Kiarl exuded was of a different dimension from Gliyak's energy. Unlike Gliyak, he had fully awakened a long time ago and could use his full strength.
Haah, haah...!
Luna exhaled roughly and glared at Kiarl. She was leaning on the axe sword Krantel on one knee, and was being protected by the former black knights.
"Just a little... please."
"Don't worry and regain your strength, even if it's for a moment, first knight."

Even in the voice of Vanessa Olson, who responded thus, the heavy breathing was noticeable. The black chaos like a bruise was visible everywhere on the bodies of the former black knights revealed between the broken armor.
If Sirone hadn't been there, they would have been annihilated already. Even though each one of them is no different from the strongest knight on the ground.
'Has father been fighting these things alone?'
After the fight began, Luna had been engulfed in astonishment so many times she couldn't even count.
She had heard some things from Sirone in advance, but once the actual battle began, her mind was completely lost.
Moreover, excluding Sirone, all attacks from the expedition have not yet inflicted a single effective blow on Kiarl. Luna and the former black knights' role was simply to protect Sirone.
'Even that makes me wonder if we are protecting father, or vice versa.'
From the back of her father who was confronting Kiarl.
Luna was feeling 'impatience'. Naturally, it was a feeling she had never experienced even once.
In fact, Sirone was fighting while controlling his increasingly impatient heart, and the reason was no different.
It was because Gliyak had awakened not in the Black Sea but in Inse at this point. Sirone judged that there were no means to stop it in Inse at this point.
If he hadn't faced Kiarl, Sirone would have retreated without a second thought.
Being unable to stop Gliyak meant no less than the extinction of the family.
There was a variable called Kinzelo, but the likelihood of them stepping up to prevent the disaster of Inse didn't seem high.
Sirone thought that eventually, Gliyak would have to be dealt with by Runcandel, Zipple, and the empire, including the abyss and the other forces.
It was the worst. However, it was impossible to leave with Kiarl in front of him, and even if it was possible, the problems that would arise after the retreat were hard to handle.
[You seem to be in a hurry... Sirone Runcandel.]
Kiarl's eyes narrowed like crescents. He was accurately seeing through Sirone's feelings.
"So you still have the leisure to care about that."
Whoosh!
A storm was brewing, the aura of Genesis gathered on Sirone's sword.
It wasn't just Sirone who was in a hurry.
Kiarl was also uncomfortable with the fact that Sirone's power had become stronger than when he had faced him in the past.
Monster.
Those who had experienced the King of the Black Sea all perceived them as monsters, but Kiarl had no choice but to see Sirone in the same way.
And the moment the aura gathered in Barisada was about to explode.
Kiarl felt something that made him lose the leisurely smile he had from Inse. Sirone also stopped his movements and his eyes widened.
'This is...!'
Just as they felt Gliyak awakening at the moment the battle was about to start.
Sirone and Kiarl were aware of the fact that a new Genesis Knight had appeared in Inse.
The only thing that could transmit that energy this far into the void was the clear light of Genesis.
Luna and the former black knights did not feel that light.
'It's Ron Hairan, him!'
It wasn't the energy of Talaries or Rosa, or other superhumans he knew. He could feel the bright energy unique to Hairan's righteousness, as if it was right in front of him.
However, for some reason, he could feel not only the energy of Hairan's righteousness from that Genesis light, but also a faint spirit energy.
'Why is the spirit energy with it... Could it be that the youngest one helped in some way? There's no reason for Solderet's energy to be embedded in Hairan's righteousness.'
He couldn't make a decision, and it wasn't an important issue at the moment.
Anyway, through that, Sirone was able to guess the situation in Inse.
'The King of the Black Sea woke up in the land of the empire, and Ron Hairan confronted him and crossed the wall. There's no other explanation.'
The Ron Hairan that Sirone knew was definitely a knight who could reach Genesis if he had a chance. He thought the possibility of falling into magic like Smarion was much higher.
Anyway, there's no reason for Sirone to hesitate in the fight with Kiarl now.
Of course, just because Ron has reached Genesis doesn't mean he can definitely subdue the fifth king of chaos, and it's even less likely that the subjugation will end without any damage to the world.
A clear hope has emerged. Moreover, if Gliyak is annihilated thanks to Ron's sword, one of his missions would be reduced.
'If he succeeds in stopping Gliyak, I must express my gratitude.'
With a grin, this time Sirone smiled.
"Wouldn't it be better to keep smiling, Kiarl? You reveal your inner thoughts too easily, you don't seem qualified to be called a king of anything."
At that moment, Luna realized that her father's sword was regaining stability... she could be sure.
This fight would end in the expedition's victory.
Has there ever been a moment of life and death that was this calm?
Until his breath stopped and his consciousness was cut off, Jin felt a strange sense of relief.
He didn't know why he could feel that way, but the reason was one.
The first thing the great man, who had newly entered the realm of the 'demi-god', did was to bestow protection on Jin.
The light of Genesis, floating in the air, was slowly approaching Ron's chest.
It scattered a light that only he could see, spoke in a language that only he could hear, and revealed a meaning that only he could understand.
At the moment of overcoming death, Ron once resisted fate. Entirely by his own will.
Therefore, the magnitude of the pure power he possessed was no different from that of Genesis at that time. That's why he was able to fight such a long battle with the Paewang sword unfolded.
But after that.
Ron's mind quickly crumbled.
He was immersed in sorrow and chaos and was dependent on his heart.
As a result, he was becoming a monster like the old ghost captain Smarion Proch.
Thanks to meeting Jin, he was able to escape from the abyss.

Those who have the power of Genesis are all at risk of becoming monsters, and that danger does not disappear even after becoming a demi-god. It always remains like a disease that can erupt at any time.
Even if they are demi-gods, they are fundamentally human and therefore cannot fully handle that power.
If the two had not met in this void, Ron would never have reached Genesis. After the war began, Ron's demonization was progressing uncontrollably.
Therefore, Gliyak was the one who gave the final kick to that demonization, and Jin was the one who stopped Ron from crossing the line until the end.
Ron slowly reached out to the light of Genesis that had stopped in front of his chest.
It was like a blazing fire. When he grabbed it with both hands, the light flowed between his fingers and came back, repeating this and giving Ron the final enlightenment.
Then Ron gently lifted a lump of that light with his hand, and made the light flow into Jin, who was bowed down.
As if ripples were rising on a calm water surface, the light of Genesis dispersed and seeped into Jin.
However, Jin could not fully absorb that lump of light. The power that Jin could absorb from it was less than one-tenth.
The remaining energy will scatter somewhere and disappear forever.
Ron didn't regret it. Rather, he was simply grateful for the fact that he could heal Jin's wounds at this cost.
The remaining light of Genesis in Ron and the energy flowing into Jin were each becoming one with the two people.
Ron's rune, which had turned black, regained its original color, and the blood pouring from Jin's wound turned red and subsided.
And the void was vibrating.
Gliyak was angry. It was incomprehensible for Gliyak why a mere human, not the terrible shadow of Solderet that he had been so wary of, was messing things up.
After all, he never permitted that human to enter here in the first place.

If he had stayed outside, he would have become an entity close to the kings of chaos like themselves. Gliyak had thought that would definitely be the case. Because he had judged that Ron was completely dependent on his heart.
Both people were soaked in the light of Genesis.
Hoo...
Then, a breath escaped from Jin's lips.
It was not the dark, damp breath of death, but a clear and clean breath as if a new life was being born.
All the wounds were healed. The light of Genesis was fundamentally different from the legacy of Numerus, so the internal injuries were not completely healed, but Jin felt his body was very light.

The chaos that had been enhancing energy mixed with the spirit was also completely gone. Therefore, his martial arts returned to their original state, but it didn't matter at all. It was a power he had to use against Ron.
There were some black traces of chaos left like freckles all over his body, but that was not a problem either.
Jin did not see the moment he was healed himself.
Nevertheless, he felt he could understand what had happened without needing Ron's explanation.
"Jin."
Jin grabbed Ron's outstretched hand and stood up. The light of Genesis, which Jin could not see until a while ago, was causing a faint radiance in Ron's body.
"Lord Ron."
The two stared at each other in silence for a while.
Like comrades who have fought together for a long time, they felt like they could see each other's inner selves.
"If it weren't for you, I would have become a monster and killed Dante with my own hands. And I wouldn't have felt the sadness and pain from that."
At those words, Jin's pupils dilated.
It was because Ron was still talking as if Dante was alive.
